title: End-of-Life Vehicles Regulation (EU) 2026/1738
notes: Recorded with no bindings, deliberately: the act exists and creates a Digital Circularity Vehicle Passport, and we hold no vehicle product group to bind it to. An instrument that reaches nothing we model is still worth holding — it is how the catalog stops the act being rediscovered as new, and it is the shape a horizontal act takes before its groups are known. Full requirements cover passenger cars and light commercial vans, with a reduced end-of-life-treatment set for heavy-duty vehicles, motorcycles and special-purpose vehicles. The passport date is now sourced, read from the OJ text: Art. 13(1) — 'From 1 September 2032, each vehicle placed on the market shall have a Digital Circularity Vehicle Passport'. An earlier secondary source gave 'two years after entry into force', i.e. around August 2028; that is the Regulation's general application date under Art. 59(2) and not the passport date, which is four years later. The manifest previously recorded no date at all rather than an unsourced one, which was the right call. Note also that 'digital product passport' appears zero times in this Regulation — the Digital Circularity Vehicle Passport is a differently-named instrument, not an ESPR DPP, though Art. 13(1) requires it to be aligned and interoperable with the Art. 77 battery passport and with passports established under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781. This Regulation amends four acts, not two: its title names Regulations (EU) No 168/2013, (EU) 2018/858, (EU) 2019/1020 and (EU) 2023/1542 — Art. 53 amends the Batteries Regulation (applies 13 Aug 2026), Art. 54 amends 2019/1020 (applies 1 Sep 2028), Art. 55 amends 2018/858 and 168/2013 (applies 1 Sep 2032). Scope is staged if a vehicle group is ever modelled: Art. 2(1) takes M1 and N1 first, special-purpose M1/N1 from 1 Sep 2029, and M2, M3, N2, N3, O and L-category from 1 Sep 2031. Note the relationship with ESPR: Art. 1(2)(h) excludes vehicles only in respect of aspects already regulated by sector-specific acts, so the exclusion is partial and aspect-scoped, and this Regulation is the automotive passport route.
